glossary.title: Property Analyser Glossary
glossary.subtitle: Quick definitions for the calculator inputs and outputs.

noi.title: NOI
noi.body: Net Operating Income. Rent minus operating expenses before debt service.

capRate.title: Cap Rate
capRate.body: Annual NOI divided by purchase price. Shows unlevered return.

cashOnCash.title: Cash on Cash
cashOnCash.body: Annual cash flow divided by cash invested (down payment + closing + reno).

vacancy.title: Vacancy Rate
vacancy.body: Percent of time the property is expected to be unoccupied.

maintenance.title: Maintenance %
maintenance.body: Reserve for repairs and replacements as a percent of income.

dscr.title: DSCR
dscr.body: Debt Service Coverage Ratio. NOI divided by debt service.

glossary.title: BUYD Glossary
glossary.subtitle: Key terms used in the BUYD calculator.

ltv.title: LTV
ltv.body: Loan-to-Value. Debt balance divided by asset value.

dscr.title: DSCR
dscr.body: Debt Service Coverage Ratio. Income divided by interest cost.

borrowCapacity.title: Borrow Capacity
borrowCapacity.body: Maximum borrowing allowed this year under target and lender LTV.

cashBuffer.title: Cash Buffer
cashBuffer.body: Reserve cash used to cover living expenses during downturns.

targetLtv.title: Target LTV
targetLtv.body: Desired leverage level used to cap new borrowing.

stressEvents.title: Stress Events
stressEvents.body: Shocks to asset value, income, interest rates, or expenses.

snowball.body: Smallest balance first. Optimizes motivation and quick wins.

hybrid.body: Attack high-rate debt above a threshold, then smallest balances.

formulas.title: Formulas
formulas.subtitle: Learn the formulas that make advice fast, clear, and confident.

roi.title: Return on Investment (ROI)
roi.example:
Example
You buy at $10,000 and sell at $12,000.
Gain is $2,000 on a $10,000 cost.
ROI = (12,000 - 10,000) / 10,000 = 20%.

compound.title: Compound interest
compound.example:
Example
You invest $10,000 at 7% for 10 years.
Growth compounds each year.
FV = 10,000 * (1.07)^10 = ~$19,672.

rule72.title: Rule of 72
rule72.example:
Example
At 8% return, 72 / 8 = 9.
That is about 9 years to double.

debtEquity.title: Debt-to-equity
debtEquity.example:
Example
Debt $200,000 and equity $100,000.
D/E = 200,000 / 100,000 = 2.0.
That means $2 of debt for every $1 of equity.

dti.title: Debt-to-income (DTI)
dti.example:
Example
Debt $1,200 and income $4,000.
DTI = 1,200 / 4,000 = 30%.
Lenders use this to judge affordability.

savingsRate.title: Savings rate
savingsRate.example:
Example
Save $800 from $4,000 income.
Savings rate = 800 / 4,000 = 20%.
Early on, this matters more than return.

cashFlow.title: Cash flow
cashFlow.use: Core survival metric; negative is a warning.
cashFlow.example:
Example
Income $5,000 minus expenses $4,200.
Cash flow = $800.
Positive cash flow keeps you in the game.

presentValue.title: Present value
presentValue.example:
Example
$10,000 in 3 years at 5%.
PV = 10,000 / (1.05)^3 = ~$8,638.
Future dollars are worth less today.

irr.title: Internal rate of return (IRR)
irr.formula: IRR is the rate where NPV = 0
irr.example:
Example
Invest $10,000 today, receive $4,000 for 3 years.
IRR is the rate that makes the NPV equal zero.
Here the IRR is about 9.7%.

npv.title: Net present value (NPV)
npv.use: Decide if a project is worth doing.
npv.example:
Example
Invest $50,000, receive $15,000 for 4 years at 8%.
NPV = discounted cash flows minus initial cost.
NPV ~ -$314, so it is slightly negative.

pe.title: Price-to-earnings (P/E)
pe.example:
Example
Price $40 and EPS $2.
P/E = 40 / 2 = 20.
This is 20 times earnings.

expectedReturn.title: Expected return
expectedReturn.example:
Example
60% at 8% and 40% at 4%.
E(R) = 0.6*8% + 0.4*4% = 6.4%.
Weighted averages tell the story.

stdev.title: Standard deviation
stdev.example:
Example
Returns of 2%, 8%, 10% move more than 5%, 6%, 7%.
More spread means higher standard deviation.

capRate.title: Cap rate
capRate.example:
Example
NOI $24,000 and value $400,000.
Cap rate = 24,000 / 400,000 = 6%.
Higher cap rate can mean more risk.

coc.title: Cash-on-cash return
coc.formula: CoC = Annual Cash Flow / Cash Invested
coc.example:
Example
Cash flow $12,000 on $100,000 invested.
CoC = 12,000 / 100,000 = 12%.
This ignores appreciation and loan paydown.

mindset.body: Clients do not hire formulas. They hire clarity, judgment, and tradeoff decisions.
